newsitem.title: THAILAND: Chavalit warns party members, plans to meet king.
newsitem.headline: Chavalit warns party members, plans to meet king.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, who is preparing for an audience with King Bhumibol Adulyadej, on Thursday warned his party about speaking about the fragile economy, a party member said.
Chavalit told a meeting of his New Aspiration Party (NAP) that party members who are not experts on the economy should not talk about it as it could cause uncertainty.

"The prime minister has warned party members who have nothing to do with economic issues not to talk too much about the issue because it would lead to public confusion," a NAP member said after the meeting.

He said Chavalit was due to meet King Bhumibol later in the day. Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya and central bank governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi were also due to attend the meeting with the highly-respected monarch.
They were expected to receive advice from the king or give him a report on the economic situation.

Although he is a constitutional monarch seen as above politics, King Bhumibol's influence over policy is critical. In the past he has intervened in times of turmoil to halt violence and prevent further unrest. His word is always heeded.
The government on Tuesday announced a series of tough austerity measures aimed at boosting the nation's economy, which has hit its slowest rate of growth in more than a decade.
The measures, imposed after receiving recommendations from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), included the shock suspension of more than half the country's finance companies.
Other measures included tough monetary and fiscal measures including a three percent rise in the value added tax, a cap on inflation and a cut in the current account deficit.

The announcement of the measures rattled financial markets and investors. Financial authorities and Chavalit met leading bankers late on Wednesday to assure them that the remaining financial institutions and banks were not in danger of collapsing.
But despite the assurances, uncertainty over the situation of the finance sector has caused jittery investors to sell stocks and drive the bourse down for the third consecutive day.
Officials said the ultimate goal of the economic measures was to obtain $12-15 billion in loans or aid from the IMF and foreign nations.
Thanong is due to go to Japan on Sunday to hold talks with banking and IMF officials.
